critiques.assumption: Agreement between parts, packing map and destination diagram establishes agreement with the accepted order.
critiques.limitation: A wrong map could accept a complete set for another layout and teach that same wrong arrangement. D2-O3/O4 establish discrepancies and confusion, but do not establish this common-source failure. Geometric outlines also need not distinguish exterior color.
critiques.opening: Check order identity independently before using the map to check physical completeness and guide placement.
critiques.comparison: The inventory silhouette detects absent or mismatched shapes; the spatial template explains destinations. Their coupling transfers one correspondence from packing to assembly, but also propagates a wrong correspondence. Z1 and Z2 can share this vulnerability if both inherit the same mistaken layout selection. A closure interlock adds physical occupancy enforcement but cannot establish that the map represents the accepted order.
critiques.probe: Deliberately swap otherwise complete layout maps between sample orders, including the same layout with a wrong exterior color. Compare shape-only checks with independent order-slip checks; these are proposed challenges, not observed failures.

openings.claim: An independently verified order-specific map may combine inventory checking and placement guidance while catching configurations that are internally consistent but wrong for the order.
openings.delta: Before loading, the second worker checks the map against the original order slip for compartment count, component requirements and exterior color; the packing worker then checks physical contents against the verified map. Both checking times count toward workshop time.
openings.prediction: Relative to A1, this should detect more swapped-map errors; relative to Z1, the retained map should help placement; relative to Z2, physical matching should expose omissions. Shared mistaken specifications or rushed second checks defeat the interaction.
openings.probe: Reuse up to 15 samples across counterbalanced challenged checks by both workers. Include map preparation and both checks in total time. Use ten participants for directional unaided-arrangement evidence. Measure actual costs and delivery feasibility before adoption; only the 60-order pilot can assess its specified completeness, time and customer-success targets.
assumptions: Original slips accurately preserve accepted choices.
Independent checking remains practical with two workers and one bench.
The unchanged footprint, stationery capacity, removable partitions, accepted counts/colors, cost caps and delivery date remain mandatory.
